Q: Thank you for agreeing to give this recorded statement. Please state your full name for the record.
A: I'd rather just keep it to what happened, if that's okay.
Q: That's fine. Can you describe where you were when the collision occurred?
A: I was driving on the main road in Baytown, Texas, heading toward the freeway. I was in the right lane and needed
to move left because the lane was ending ahead.
Q: What did you do before you changed lanes?
A: I checked my mirror and glanced over my shoulder. I saw a car a little behind me, but it looked like it was far
enough back. I put my signal on and started to move over.
Q: Did the other vehicle make contact with you?
A: Yes. The side of their car hit the rear quarter of mine. It was a scraping sort of impact, and both cars pulled slightly
toward the shoulder.
Q: How fast were you traveling at the time?
A: Maybe thirty-five or forty miles an hour. Traffic was moving steadily but not quickly.
Q: Did you stop at the scene?
A: I pulled onto the shoulder and turned on my hazards. The other driver got out and we exchagned information. The
police came out and wrote a report.
Q: Have you had any injuries from this collision?
A: My left knee took the brunt of it. It hit the door frame and I've had swelling and pain ever since. Walking up stairs is
difficult right now.
Q: Have you sought medical treatment?
A: Yes, I was seen at an urgent care clinic that same day and I've been referred to an orthopedic doctor for follow-up.
Q: Thank you. Is there anything else you'd like to add?
A: Only that I want my car repaired and my knee looked after. That's all for now.
</page>
